partner_context.their_ambition: Şehir Hatları — City Lines — is the historic public ferry operator owned by the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality. Its network crosses the Bosphorus between Europe and Asia, runs up the Golden Horn, and reaches out across the Sea of Marmara to the Princes' Islands, serving tens of millions of commuter, island and visitor journeys a year from more than fifty piers.
partner_context.their_pressure: The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality is bringing battery-electric ferries into the Şehir Hatları fleet, modernising the historic vapur service toward the city's clean-transport goals. Growth and the net-zero mandate both demand fleet renewal without disturbing the services people rely on today.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the Şehir Hatları network — fast, low-wake hops across the Bosphorus and out to the Princes' Islands that complement the city's own electrification, with conventional low-speed handling in the busy Eminönü and Golden Horn approaches.

hero.title: İstanbul Şehir Hatları (City Lines) × Navier — a zero-emission foiling layer on the water
hero.subtitle: A foiling tier above today's network on the Bosphorus, the Golden Horn and the Sea of Marmara: faster, near-silent, low-wake lines, a clear decarbonization path, and the services people rely on left running underneath.
hero.what_we_do_together: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the Şehir Hatları network — fast, low-wake hops across the Bosphorus and out to the Princes' Islands that complement the city's own electrification, with conventional low-speed handling in the busy Eminönü and Golden Horn approaches.

why_now: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the Şehir Hatları network — fast, low-wake hops across the Bosphorus and out to the Princes' Islands that complement the city's own electrification, with conventional low-speed handling in the busy Eminönü and Golden Horn approaches. The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality is bringing battery-electric ferries into the Şehir Hatları fleet, modernising the historic vapur service toward the city's clean-transport goals.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the network as the fast marine mode on the Bosphorus, the Golden Horn and the Sea of Marmara — feeding the existing rail, metro and bus interchanges and adding lines toward the authority's published growth and net-zero targets.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready — the same DNA as the autonomous road programs — built for fleet operation, with a ~100-vessel network proving the model in the Maldives.

proof_points.claim: The authority runs marine transport at public scale.
proof_points.evidence: Lines cross the Bosphorus (Eminönü – Kadıköy – Üsküdar – Beşiktaş), run the Bosphorus villages up to Anadolu Kavağı, climb the Golden Horn to Eyüp, and reach the Princes' Islands (Büyükada, Heybeliada, Burgazada, Kınalıada) across the Sea of Marmara.
proof_points.source: Şehir Hatları A.Ş., the public ferry operator owned by the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (İBB)

proof_points.claim: There is a published growth and decarbonization mandate.
proof_points.evidence: The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality is bringing battery-electric ferries into the Şehir Hatları fleet, modernising the historic vapur service toward the city's clean-transport goals.
proof_points.source: Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (İBB) electric-ferry & clean-transport program; Türkiye 2053 net-zero target

proof_points.evidence: Hydrofoiling, software-governed vessels — the same DNA arriving in autonomous road mobility — built for fleet operation.

proof_points.claim: The fleet model is real and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing proving the network model in the Maldives; 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours; a demo vessel is on the water now.

objections.concern: Does this compete with the existing public ferry service?
objections.response: No — Navier is a passenger-only foiling layer above the existing service, adding fast frequencies on the busy corridors the conventional boats can't run economically. It complements the electrification already underway.
Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at existing piers — no new shore power, vertiports or rights-of-way.

objections.concern: Is foiling safe in busy, shared public waterways?
objections.response: Foiling is software-governed — geofenced no-foil and low-wake zones near piers, ferry lanes and moorings, automatic speed and wake limits in shared water, and conventional low-speed handling everywhere it isn't cleared to fly.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet (Pioneer II + long-range hybrid), the Maldives-proven network playbook, certification and operations.
the_ask.partner_brings: Network integration, berth access, the published network mandate and regulatory cover.
the_ask.next_step: A pilot on the busiest corridors, co-specified with the authority against its published network and net-zero targets.

close.title: A zero-emission water layer that grows with the city.
close.body: Start on the busiest corridors, scale across the full network, then mature the service — a zero-emission foiling tier that advances the authority's net-zero mandate while the services people rely on keep running underneath.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop — roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — the open water and the piers already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the long-range hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the charging excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.
